main_text.p: mia & pœnæ. Id uerũ esse,uel ex ijs quæ ὡς ἐν τύπῳ subijciam,manifestum fit.

1. Sæpe bonorum caussa, etiam improbis bene est. ut Soaritis pepercit Deus, Lothi hospitis caussa: Gen.19.v.20.21. Ac nihil dubium est,piorum caussa uel miti-gare Deũ,uel auferre ingentia mala: interdum & pœnas publicas differre. Ita Deus dicitur benefecisse Potipharo Ægy ptio propter Iosephum seruum eius: & pœnas publicas distulisse donec uixit pi-us Rex Iosias.

2 Interdum improbis male est propter pios. Vt cum illi inuidia & odio marce-scũt,& seipsos excruciant. Iuxta dictum: Ecce iste concepit iniquitatem,prægnans est dolore,& pariet rem inanem. Puteũ fodit,& effodit eum,& cecidit in foueam quam fecit. Reuertetur molestia eius in caput eius: &supra uerticem eius iniu-ria eius descendet: Psal.7.14.15.16.

Aut cũ in operibus manuum suarũ il-laqueati, iusto Dei iudicio, tragicas sce-lerum & machinationum suarum pœnas dant. Vt Danielis accusatores, tandem, mandatu Darij Regis, præcipitati in la-cum leonum,unà cum uxoribus & libe-ris

page.notes: Catchword absent. The faint stain and show-through at the left edge are not transcribed. Doubtful: "pœnas publicas distulisse" and "supra uerticem" are read from a small, slightly blurred scan; "pariet" and "prægnans" are as printed (prægnans with the ę-style ligature). The Greek phrase "ὡς ἐν τύπῳ" is reproduced as best read from the scan; the accent placement is uncertain. Line "Reuertetur" continues to the printed text as shown. Printing irregularities such as "Iosias" for Iosias and "Potipharo Ægy ptio" split across the line are left as printed.
